name: Homestead
overview: Scripture in Leviticus 25 outlines God's provision for maintaining family homesteads through laws concerning redemption and possession. When a brother becomes poor and sells his land, close kin have the right to redeem it, preserving the inheritance within the family (Leviticus 25:25-27). If no one else can redeem the property, the original owner may do so, provided he can restore the value (Leviticus 25:26-27). However, if redemption is not possible, the property remains with the buyer until the year of Jubilee, when it reverts to the original owner, ensuring the land is not permanently alienated (Leviticus 25:28). Special provisions apply to houses within walled cities, which may be redeemed within a year; if not redeemed, they become the permanent possession of the buyer and do not return in the Jubilee (Leviticus 25:29-30). These instructions emphasize God's design for family stability and stewardship of land across generations.
